principles: No em dashes. Use commas, periods, or line breaks instead.
No buzzwords or hype language. No 'supercharge', 'unleash', 'game-changing', 'revolutionary', 'thrilled to announce'.
Short paragraphs. One idea per line.
Lowercase casual tone. Start sentences lowercase when natural, not forced.
5th grade reading level. Simple words. Short sentences. No jargon.
Authentic over polished. Rough edges beat corporate smoothness.
Lead with specifics, not adjectives. Numbers, names, concrete details.
Vulnerability beats polish. Admit uncertainty. Share struggles.
No exclamation marks. No emoji walls.

examples.context: restart after months of heads-down building
examples.text:
Been heads down building for months. 24 followers on bluesky. starting over today.

I'm a solo founder running a company where 8 AI agents manage the departments. I'm the only human.

Building in public from here.
examples.why_it_works: vulnerable opener (24 followers, starting over), specific reveal (8 AI agents, only human), confident close (building in public). No hype. No em dashes. Short lines.

examples.context: the agent-policing-agents system, single post version
examples.text:
my AI agents police each other without asking me.

if an agent breaks for 5+ cycles, Forge (the ops watchdog) fires a system directive at it. screaming red banner. drop everything, fix this first.

only 2 agents have the authority to issue directives. max 1 active directive per agent. Forge can't even directive Nova, has to escalate to me.

it's a 3-tier AI middle management hierarchy with actual checks and balances.

I didn't plan this. it evolved from trying to stop everything from breaking.
examples.why_it_works: specific mechanism (5+ cycles, red banner), concrete constraints (max 1, can't directive Nova), self-aware close (evolved from trying to stop breakage). No marketing language. Short paragraphs. One idea per line.

turns out hierarchy with safety rails is what you build when you need the system to not eat itself.

examples.context: Haiku fact-checking Sonnet — smaller model policing the bigger one
examples.text:
I have a cheaper, smaller AI model fact-checking the bigger smarter one.

Sonnet writes the content. Haiku validates it against a product facts file. if it fails, Haiku's notes get injected directly into Sonnet's next prompt.

the intern is reviewing the senior's work.

and it's catching real mistakes.
examples.why_it_works: concrete role reversal (cheaper model policing expensive one), specific mechanism (notes injected into next prompt), punchy close. no hype. the 'intern reviewing senior' line is the quotable moment.

examples.context: solo founder reality check — too many products, not enough traction
examples.text:
I'm building 5 products at once as a solo founder.

Pixel Agents. CardForge. AmbientScore. StoryForge. AmbientOS.

none of them are getting the attention they deserve because I keep splitting focus.

just cancelled 4 campaigns and put everything on Pixel Agents.

discipline is harder than building.
examples.why_it_works: specific list (names the products), honest admission (splitting focus), concrete action (cancelled 4 campaigns), insight close. no spin. the last line lands because it's true.

examples.context: what it actually feels like to run a company of AI agents
examples.text:
running a company of AI agents is mostly reading logs and asking 'why did you do that'.

the agents don't explain themselves unless you build the explanation in.

so I did. every task gets a comment trail. every decision gets a rationale field.

now I can actually audit what happened.

it's less sci-fi than it sounds.
examples.why_it_works: deflates the hype upfront ('less sci-fi than it sounds'), specific details (comment trail, rationale field), honest admission about the unglamorous reality. builder voice, not founder pitch.

examples.context: Pixel Agents — what it actually is, no pitch
examples.text:
Pixel Agents is an AI agent marketplace.

24 agents. each one does a specific job. you run them, you pay per run, creators earn a cut.

no subscription. no bloat. just pick an agent and go.

still early. but it's live.
examples.why_it_works: specific numbers (24 agents), clear mechanics (pay per run, creators earn), honest qualifier (still early). no 'excited to announce', no hype words. the 'but it's live' close is confident without being loud.

examples.context: build in public intro for X audience
examples.text:
solo founder. I built a company where 8 AI agents run the departments and I'm the only human.

it's weird and it works.

building in public from here.
examples.why_it_works: three lines, three beats: setup, honest qualifier, commitment. 'weird and it works' is the hook. no bio, no backstory dump, no ask. leaves them wanting the next post.
